subject: Granular metering: long-context sessions & minimum billing
messages:
From: Sam Walker <sam.walker@soundify.io>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify billing for long-running sessions and minimums

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Soundify is excited about the latency and multitenant routing bits. Before we move to procurement, procurement asked a couple of specific clarifications on metering:

1) We have long user sessions (some up to 30k tokens accumulated via chat history + files). Do you meter against the total historical context length or the active request window?
2) If we store conversation context on our side and only send deltas, how does that affect minimum-billing units?
3) Are there rounding/minimums per-request or per-minute that might surprise us during heavy streaming?

They also asked whether we can get a small committed discount if we pick the dedicated plan — they'd like a simple example bill to show finance. Any quick examples you can send would help.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Walker
Head of Product, Soundify
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Walker <sam.walker@soundify.io>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-01T10:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify billing for long-running sessions and minimums

Hi Sam — great questions. Short answers up front, then I’ll attach an example invoice and a one-page metering explainer.

- We meter tokens per request (ingest + generated tokens). The platform supports prefix/KV caching; cached tokens do not count if they’re handled entirely by our KV layer without being sent over the wire.
- If you keep the full history client-side and only send deltas, you’re billed on the tokens actually transmitted/processed by Redwood.
- Rounding: billing is aggregated per-minute for streaming calls and per-request for non-streaming; we apply a 10-token minimum per request and round up to the nearest 10-token increment for metering.

I’m looping in Lauren from pricing to make sure the example numbers are conservative for procurement. I’ll follow up with a brief worked example and a draft SOW including a committed discount tier for Dedicated.

Best,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-02T08:07:00-07:00
Subject: RE: metering rounding + discount proposal (internal)

Folks — quick internal note before I draft numbers for Sam/procurement. A few edge cases I want to confirm:

1) Long streaming sessions that send sporadic deltas: are we currently applying the per-minute aggregation only when a single streaming connection is active, or do we collapse multiple short streams from the same session into the same minute window? Example: user has websocket open for 2 hours but only sends input every ~8 minutes.
2) Minimums: default 10-token floor per non-stream request. For streaming, we bill tokens emitted per minute with 1-minute granularity and then round up to the nearest 10-token boundary per minute. That can create a small overhead for sparse activity — do we want to propose an explicit per-session smoothing discount for customers that maintain long-lived connections (e.g., 5% off the aggregated minute-rounding overhead for sessions > 60 minutes)?
3) When customers supply their own KV cache and we honor a cache-hit locally (no call to model), there should be zero billing. Need to confirm behavior when client sends a cache fingerprint but server still validates — does the validation cost tokens?

Aditya, can you confirm the implementation details (especially #1 and #3) so I can finalize the sample pricing and an opt-in smoothing concession for Soundify?

-L
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-02T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: metering rounding + discount proposal (internal)

Lauren, Marcus — answers below (from infra/pricing implementation notes):

1) Streaming aggregation: we aggregate on a per-connection basis. If Soundify keeps a single websocket per user, tokens are counted against that single connection; sporadic deltas are billed in the minute buckets where data is transmitted. We do not automatically collapse separate connections (e.g., mobile and web) unless they share the same session id and are multiplexed by the client.

2) Minimums/rounding: correct — 10-token floor per non-stream request. Streaming is billed per-minute buckets; each minute’s total is rounded up to nearest 10-token increment. We can optionally apply a per-session smoothing credit to refund a calculated rounding overhead on a monthly invoice (not real-time). Implementation-wise it’s a post-process adjustment.

3) KV/cache: if the customer provides a client-side cache fingerprint and the request short-circuits locally (no model invocation), we charge zero. If the server validates the fingerprint with a lightweight hash check that does not invoke model execution, the validation itself is free (no billed tokens) — only tokens processed by the model count.

One more note: multi-part requests where you send attachments for embedding plus context text are billed across both embedding and generation units in the single request; the platform attributes tokens to the corresponding operation but aggregates in the same minute window for streaming.

- A
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Walker <sam.walker@soundify.io>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@soundify.io
Date: 2027-10-04T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify billing for long-running sessions and minimums

Hi Sam / Soundify procurement team — following up with the concrete examples and proposal we discussed. Attached: redwood_metering_summary_v2.pdf (worked examples), soundify_usage_samples.csv (toy data you provided, run through our metering), and a draft SOW. Key points:

- Metering: only tokens transmitted to/processed by Redwood are billed. Cached tokens that never reach the model are free.
- Long sessions: if you open a persistent websocket, billing is aggregated per connection per-minute; sparse traffic will be billed in the minute buckets where data moved. Example: 2-hour open ws that sent 8 discrete user messages (avg 120 tokens each) results in billing for the minutes those messages hit, rounded to nearest 10-token increment. The post-process smoothing concession (described below) can offset the rounding overhead.
- Discount: for a 12-month Dedicated commitment at $X/mo baseline (numbers in the attached SOW), we’re proposing: 8% committed usage credit + an optional rounding-smoothing concession that refunds up to 5% of aggregated minute-level rounding overhead (applied monthly, capped at $Y). This concession is opt-in and intended for workloads with long-lived connections and sparse deltas.

Please review the attachments. If that looks reasonable, Lauren will work with procurement on formal language and DocuSign. Happy to hop on a short call to walk through one of the sample rows from your CSV.

Thanks,
Marcus

- For the smoothing concession, can you show a sample monthly invoice line that demonstrates how the rounding refund would appear (simple before/after numbers)?

If you can get those two small items into the attached PDF and SOW tomorrow we’ll escalate to finance and legal. Appreciate the responsiveness — Sam
